parsed.summary: The Lean theorem is a one-step, coefficient-level statement about a single harmonic, under many structural hypotheses. A corrected linear wave is built from a source in WaveClass α. The theorem proves three things: the 'good' part lies in WaveClass (α + 1/2 − 3κ); an excluded-slot error lies in UnweightedClass for every real N; and an exact pointwise identity holds, residual + source·carrier = (good + error)·carrier. Paper Proposition 9.3 is a statement about the full iterated construction (u^[j], p^[j]), and the pairing may be loose. It covers the physical decomposition R = G + F, harmonic support structure, the physical flat bound |F|_m ≤ C q^N, and exact mean equations. Lean captures at most a single-step analogue of the 'G + F with F flat' part. Key caveats: (iii) and most of (i) are not formalized, and several hypotheses (ExactConditions on the corrected coefficients, hsolve, a band-independent radius) assume properties of the construction.

glossary.standard_concept: local geometric/angular conditions for the exact residual identity

lean_claims.plain:
Assume the following hypotheses:
- InputBounds s P α κ d a, and κ ≤ 1/2.
- A slot family g with linear(fastScale·fast) = 1/length.
- Flat edges and band-scale control data.
- source ∈ WaveClass s P α.
- A Gaussian bound P_n(x) ≤ exp(−c(coord_n(x) − 1/2)^2 · length_n) with c > 0.
- A band-independent radius R.
- Polynomial jet bounds on the normal, and 0 < b ≤ |normal| ≤ M on the domain.
- 1/frequency_n bounded by ε_n^{1/2} times a slow polynomial.
- principal = −source on the domain.
- ExactConditions for the corrected coefficients.
Then three conclusions hold:
(1) constructedGood ∈ WaveClass s P (α + 1/2 − 3κ);
(2) the excluded-slot error lies in UnweightedClass s N for every real N;
(3) for all n and x in the domain, harmonicResidual(corrected)_n(x) + source_n(x)·carrier = (constructedGood_n(x) + error_n(x))·carrier.

paper_claims.plain: After any finite sequence of the construction steps, with pressure reconstructed, the physical residual decomposes as R(u^[j], p^[j]) = G^[j] + F^[j]. (i) The nonzero harmonics of G* are a finite band-independent set of harmonics, with supported smooth coefficients in W_α and mean in M_µ. (ii) |F^[j]|_m ≤ C_{j,m,N} q^N for all m and N, uniformly over bands, labels and points. (iii) Exact mean equations (9.6) hold.

coverage.why: Lean treats one wave-construction step for one harmonic coefficient, not the finite iterated sequence with pressure reconstruction.
Only the W-class membership of the good coefficient is formalized, with an explicit exponent α + 1/2 − 3κ. The finite harmonic set H_j, supports and smooth zero extension are not formalized.
Lean gives UnweightedClass for all N at coefficient level. Whether this equals the physical |F|_m ≤ C q^N uniform bound cannot be checked, because UnweightedClass is not shown.

flags.explanation: The paper result concerns the full iterated construction and the physical residual R(u^[j], p^[j]), with parts (i)–(iii). Lean is a single-step coefficient identity. The excerpt's proof mentions Propositions 9.1, 7.2, 6.6, so the Lean statement may better match one of those (e.g. a pulse-inverse step). Part (iii) and the support/harmonic-finiteness claims of (i) are absent.

hg assumes ExactConditions for a.corrected s d g.cutoff, i.e. smoothness, angular invariance and radial normalization of the constructed (output) coefficients. The paper presents these as properties of the construction, not as hypotheses. If they are not discharged elsewhere, the result is conditional on them.

flags.explanation: hR forces a.radius to be the same function R for every band n. hsolve requires principal = −source exactly. hP imposes a Gaussian bound on P. These are plausible setup properties, but this is not in excerpt.

The flat-error claim relies on UnweightedClass, and the goodness claim on WaveClass and InputBounds; none of these is shown. It cannot be verified that UnweightedClass s N encodes all-derivative bounds |·|_m ≤ C q^N uniform over bands, labels and points. It might, for instance, fix the derivative order or use a different small parameter.
